Opportunity to outrank by being more technically precise about Lean 4 workflows, specifications, proof checking, and where formal verification does not apply.
Introductory article updated March 31, 2026, explaining Leanstral for a broad AI/business audience.
Emphasizes the shift from hoping code works to verifying it against strict rules in Lean 4.
Covers basic benefits for mathematicians, developers, and high-risk software teams.
Thin on implementation details; a stronger guide should add practical Lean 4 setup, workflow examples, evaluation criteria, and limitations.

stats.fact: Mistral announced Leanstral on March 16, 2026 as an open-source Lean 4 code agent; Mistral says it is trained for realistic formal repositories, released under Apache 2.0, and available through Mistral Vibe/API access.
The Mistral model card lists Leanstral 26.03 as a Labs model with 119B total parameters, 6.5B active parameters, 256k context, and model id labs-leanstral-2603.

The Hugging Face model card lists Leanstral-2603 under Apache 2.0 and describes key architecture details: MoE with 128 experts, 4 active per token, 119B parameters, 6.5B activated per token, multimodal input, and 256k context.

Mistral reports FLTEval results where Leanstral pass@2 scores 26.3 at about $36, compared with Claude Sonnet 4.6 at 23.7 and about $549; pass@16 reaches 31.9, while Claude Opus 4.6 remains higher quality but much more expensive.

Lean describes itself as an open-source programming language and proof assistant for correct, maintainable, formally verified code; its site highlights a minimal trusted kernel, extensibility, Mathlib, Cedar, Veil, Aeneas, and Fermat's Last Theorem as real-world applications.

Lean creator Leonardo de Moura argues that AI-era verification needs a separate verification layer, a small trusted kernel, reproducible proof checking, and open control outside any single model vendor.

Sonar's January 2026 State of Code survey says AI accounts for 42% of committed code among surveyed developers, developers expect 65% by 2027, 96% do not fully trust AI-generated code, and only 48% always check AI-assisted code before committing.
Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey reports 47.1% of respondents use AI tools daily and 17.7% weekly, while 46% distrust AI tool accuracy versus 33% who trust it.

GitHub Octoverse 2025 reports more than 180 million developers on GitHub, 43.2 million pull requests merged per month, nearly 1 billion commits in 2025, and about 80% of new developers using Copilot within their first week.
Veracode's Spring 2026 GenAI code security update says even top reasoning-model outputs still leave roughly a 28-30% vulnerability rate in tested AI-generated snippets.

Cloud Security Alliance's 2026 research note cites Georgia Tech tracking 35 CVEs in March 2026 directly attributable to AI coding tools, estimates the true ecosystem count could be 5-10x higher, and cites 45% AI-generated security-test failures in Veracode's longitudinal research.

angles: Spec-first coding: the important shift is not 'AI writes correct code' but 'humans and AI write precise specs, then a small trusted kernel checks proofs.'
Leanstral is best explained as a proof-engineering agent, not a generic replacement for code review.
Separate the generator from the verifier: the trust boundary is Lean's kernel and proof checker, not the LLM's confidence.

Use formal verification where correctness is local, expensive to test, or safety/security-critical; do not promise it solves product requirements, UX, integration bugs, threat modeling, or vague specs.
Cost/performance is the distinctive Leanstral claim: sparse MoE, 6.5B active parameters, FLTEval, and lower reported benchmark cost versus closed agents.
AI-code verification debt is now a credible hook: adoption is high, trust is low, and manual review cannot scale with AI output.
A practical guide should include a minimal Lean 4 mental model: theorem, specification, implementation, proof, kernel, tactic, Mathlib, lake project, and LSP feedback loop.
Trending skepticism: formal proof verifies conformance to the spec, so bad or incomplete specifications remain the main failure mode.
